claims.claimText: EPF Scheme 2026: India Replaces 74-Year-Old Retirement Law Under New Social Security Code
claims.normalizedText: epf scheme 2026 india replaces 74yearold retirement law under new social security code

claims.claimText: India's retirement framework underwent its most significant legal overhaul in seven decades when the EPF Scheme 2026 replaced the 1952 scheme effective June 29, replacing two legacy pension schemes and bringing 8 crore+ subscribers under the Code on Social Security, 2020. While the headline contribution rate stays at 12% and the interest rate at 8.25%, the new framework introduces stricter governance for exempted trusts, consolidates 13 withdrawal categories into 3, mandates 20-day pension claim settlement with 12% interest penalty for delays, and gives the government power to temporarily defer contributions during national emergencies. For most subscribers, nothing changes on day one — but the compliance architecture has been rewritten.

claims.claimText: What is the EPF Scheme 2026?: The Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026, notified on June 29, 2026, replaces the 74-year-old EPF Scheme 1952 as the legal framework governing provident fund contributions, accounts, and withdrawals for India's organised-sector workforce. It is the first major overhaul of EPF law and brings the scheme under the Code on Social Security, 2020.
claims.normalizedText: what epf scheme 2026 employees provident funds scheme 2026 notified june 29 2026 replaces 74yearold epf scheme 1952 as legal framework governing provident fund contributions accounts and withdrawals indias organisedsector workforce it first major overhaul epf law and brings scheme under code social security 2020

claims.claimText: Do I need to take any action as an existing EPF member?: No. Existing EPF subscribers under the 1952 scheme automatically become members under the 2026 scheme. Your UAN, account balance, and accumulated benefits continue without interruption. There is no requirement to re-register or submit new documents.
claims.normalizedText: do i need take any action as existing epf member no existing epf subscribers under 1952 scheme automatically become members under 2026 scheme your uan account balance and accumulated benefits continue without interruption there no requirement reregister or submit new documents

claims.claimText: What actually changed for employees?: The contribution rate (12%), wage ceiling (₹15,000), and interest rate (8.25%) remain unchanged. The main changes are: 13 partial withdrawal categories simplified to 3 (illness, education-marriage, housing); stricter governance for exempted private PF trusts; digital compliance formalized; and the government can temporarily reduce contributions during national emergencies.
claims.normalizedText: what actually changed employees contribution rate 12 wage ceiling 15000 and interest rate 825 remain unchanged main changes 13 partial withdrawal categories simplified 3 illness educationmarriage housing stricter governance exempted private pf trusts digital compliance formalized and government can temporarily reduce contributions during national emergencies

claims.claimText: What changed for pension (EPS)?: EPS 2026 replaces EPS-95 and the 1971 Family Pension Scheme. The pension formula, minimum pension (₹1,000), and contribution structure (8.33% employer) stay the same. Key improvements: pension claims must be settled within 20 days; EPFO pays 12% interest penalty for delays; and the higher-pension framework (post-Supreme Court) now has firmer statutory footing.
claims.normalizedText: what changed pension eps eps 2026 replaces eps95 and 1971 family pension scheme pension formula minimum pension 1000 and contribution structure 833 employer stay same key improvements pension claims must be settled within 20 days epfo pays 12 interest penalty delays and higherpension framework postsupreme court now has firmer statutory footing

claims.claimText: Is the EPF interest rate changing under the new scheme?: No. The EPF interest rate remains at 8.25% for FY 2025-26, as recommended by the EPFO Central Board of Trustees in March 2026. The rate is set annually and is independent of the scheme change. EPF has consistently outperformed bank FDs by 1.75-2% annually.
claims.normalizedText: epf interest rate changing under new scheme no epf interest rate remains 825 fy 202526 as recommended by epfo central board trustees march 2026 rate set annually and independent scheme change epf has consistently outperformed bank fds by 1752 annually

claims.claimText: What is the VISHWAS and AMNESTY compliance window?: The EPF Scheme 2026 introduces three time-bound compliance windows: (1) Enrolment Campaign — deadline October 31, 2026 for enrolling previously uncovered employees; (2) VISHWAS — voluntary disclosure of disputed damages; (3) AMNESTY — for informal PF trusts to regularize compliance. These are available for 6 months from notification, extendable by 6 more.
claims.normalizedText: what vishwas and amnesty compliance window epf scheme 2026 introduces three timebound compliance windows 1 enrolment campaign deadline october 31 2026 enrolling previously uncovered employees 2 vishwas voluntary disclosure disputed damages 3 amnesty informal pf trusts regularize compliance these available 6 months from notification extendable by 6 more

claims.claimText: How does the government's emergency power to reduce contributions work?: The new scheme allows the central government to temporarily reduce or defer EPF contributions for up to 3 months during pandemics, epidemics, and national disasters. This provision did not exist under the 1952 scheme. It provides fiscal flexibility during crises without permanently changing the contribution structure.
claims.normalizedText: how does governments emergency power reduce contributions work new scheme allows central government temporarily reduce or defer epf contributions up 3 months during pandemics epidemics and national disasters this provision did not exist under 1952 scheme it provides fiscal flexibility during crises without permanently changing contribution structure

claims.claimText: What happens to exempted PF trusts under the new scheme?: Exempted private PF trusts face significantly stricter governance: mandatory electronic accounting, annual audits, dematerialised investments, investment reporting, online disclosures, penalties for delayed reporting, and formal procedures for renewing exemptions. Trusts cannot declare interest rates exceeding the central government rate by more than 2%.
claims.normalizedText: what happens exempted pf trusts under new scheme exempted private pf trusts face significantly stricter governance mandatory electronic accounting annual audits dematerialised investments investment reporting online disclosures penalties delayed reporting and formal procedures renewing exemptions trusts cannot declare interest rates exceeding central government rate by more than 2

externalVerifications.claimText: What is the EPF Scheme 2026?: The Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026, notified on June 29, 2026, replaces the 74-year-old EPF Scheme 1952 as the legal framework governing provident fund contributions, accounts, and withdrawals for India's organised-sector workforce. It is the first major overhaul of EPF law and brings the scheme under the Code on Social Security, 2020.
externalVerifications.comparisonDetails: Factual assertion verified against cited source and story context.

externalVerifications.claimText: Do I need to take any action as an existing EPF member?: No. Existing EPF subscribers under the 1952 scheme automatically become members under the 2026 scheme. Your UAN, account balance, and accumulated benefits continue without interruption. There is no requirement to re-register or submit new documents.
externalVerifications.comparisonDetails: Factual assertion verified against cited source and story context.

externalVerifications.claimText: What actually changed for employees?: The contribution rate (12%), wage ceiling (₹15,000), and interest rate (8.25%) remain unchanged. The main changes are: 13 partial withdrawal categories simplified to 3 (illness, education-marriage, housing); stricter governance for exempted private PF trusts; digital compliance formalized; and the government can temporarily reduce contributions during national emergencies.
externalVerifications.comparisonDetails: Factual assertion verified against cited source and story context.

externalVerifications.claimText: What changed for pension (EPS)?: EPS 2026 replaces EPS-95 and the 1971 Family Pension Scheme. The pension formula, minimum pension (₹1,000), and contribution structure (8.33% employer) stay the same. Key improvements: pension claims must be settled within 20 days; EPFO pays 12% interest penalty for delays; and the higher-pension framework (post-Supreme Court) now has firmer statutory footing.
externalVerifications.comparisonDetails: Factual assertion verified against cited source and story context.

externalVerifications.claimText: Is the EPF interest rate changing under the new scheme?: No. The EPF interest rate remains at 8.25% for FY 2025-26, as recommended by the EPFO Central Board of Trustees in March 2026. The rate is set annually and is independent of the scheme change. EPF has consistently outperformed bank FDs by 1.75-2% annually.
externalVerifications.comparisonDetails: Factual assertion verified against cited source and story context.

externalVerifications.claimText: What is the VISHWAS and AMNESTY compliance window?: The EPF Scheme 2026 introduces three time-bound compliance windows: (1) Enrolment Campaign — deadline October 31, 2026 for enrolling previously uncovered employees; (2) VISHWAS — voluntary disclosure of disputed damages; (3) AMNESTY — for informal PF trusts to regularize compliance. These are available for 6 months from notification, extendable by 6 more.
externalVerifications.comparisonDetails: Factual assertion verified against cited source and story context.

externalVerifications.claimText: How does the government's emergency power to reduce contributions work?: The new scheme allows the central government to temporarily reduce or defer EPF contributions for up to 3 months during pandemics, epidemics, and national disasters. This provision did not exist under the 1952 scheme. It provides fiscal flexibility during crises without permanently changing the contribution structure.
externalVerifications.comparisonDetails: Factual assertion verified against cited source and story context.

externalVerifications.claimText: What happens to exempted PF trusts under the new scheme?: Exempted private PF trusts face significantly stricter governance: mandatory electronic accounting, annual audits, dematerialised investments, investment reporting, online disclosures, penalties for delayed reporting, and formal procedures for renewing exemptions. Trusts cannot declare interest rates exceeding the central government rate by more than 2%.
externalVerifications.comparisonDetails: Factual assertion verified against cited source and story context.
